title: An addendum to my last video- because some people just don’t seem to ...
transcript: We need to talk about these Hamilton screenings because the amount of comments that I am getting saying something to the effect of well if you don't want people to sing along, you can just watch it at home on Disney Plus. And I just want to put this into perspective for some people cause I don't think that is a good argument. For starters, it assumes that the only reason someone would wanna see a movie in theaters versus at home is that they can sing along. Which 1. You can sing along at home if you want, and 2. There are so many reasons why a person might wanna see the movie in theaters. It's far better quality, it's on a much bigger screen, and just by nature of being in a theater with other people, it is much closer to the experience you would get watching the show in person on Broadway versus on your couch. I would compare it to going out to eat at a restaurant versus ordering delivery from that same restaurant. Yes, it is the exact same food, but it's a completely different experience. And it would be silly of me to get up in the middle of the restaurant and start singing and then say well if you don't want to hear me sing, you should have just ordered delivery. Like, that's just not logical. And some people seem to think that because they were given permission to sing along, that means They could do whatever they want. And I've seen so many reports of people at screenings where audience members are just being completely rowdy. Not just singing along, but literally screaming, climbing over seats, dancing in front of the screen, making a mess. And that is not what a sing along is. I shouldn't even have to say this, but if you go to a sing along screening, you need to stay in your seat the whole time, and you should sing at a normal level. This is not an opportunity for you to make this about yourself. And I'm just a little confused because obviously we all understand that if you went to see Hamilton on Broadway, you would not be getting up out of your seat to film a TikTok trend in the middle of the show. I'm not sure why people feel like movie screenings are any different. It is still just as distracting to the people around you.
